concepts.title: Story Comprehension
concepts.description: Reading narrative texts to identify characters, setting, and the sequence of events (plot).
key_ideas: Identifying main and supporting characters
Understanding the setting (time and place)
Sequencing events (Beginning, Middle, End)
Answering 'Who', 'Where', and 'When' questions

concepts.title: Picture and Poster Comprehension
concepts.description: Extracting specific information from visual texts such as posters, advertisements, or picture compositions.
key_ideas: Observing visual details carefully
Connecting images with accompanying text
Understanding the purpose of a poster or notice
Answering factual questions based on visual data

concepts.title: Vocabulary Context Clues
concepts.description: Deducing the meaning of unfamiliar words by analyzing the surrounding words and sentences.
key_ideas: Using synonyms or antonyms in the text as hints
Inferring meaning from the general situation
Replacing the difficult word to test meaning
Ignoring irrelevant words to focus on the main message

concepts.title: Identifying Main Idea and Title
concepts.description: Distinguishing between the central theme of a passage and specific supporting details to choose appropriate titles.
key_ideas: Identifying the topic sentence
Differentiating between the 'big picture' and small details
Selecting a suitable title for a passage
Summarizing the text in one sentence

concepts.title: Drawing Inferences
concepts.description: Understanding implied information and drawing conclusions that are not explicitly stated in the text.
key_ideas: Reading between the lines
Using text evidence to support a guess
Predicting what might happen next based on clues
Understanding character feelings not directly described

concepts.title: Collective Nouns
concepts.description: Introduction to specific names given to groups of people, animals, or things.
key_ideas: Definition of collective nouns
Common animal groups (e.g., flock, herd, pride)
Common object groups (e.g., bunch, pack, set)

concepts.title: Pronouns — Personal and Possessive
concepts.description: Using words to replace nouns to avoid repetition and indicate ownership.
key_ideas: Subject pronouns (I, he, she, they)
Object pronouns (me, him, her, them)
Possessive pronouns (mine, yours, ours)

concepts.title: Adverbs — Modifying Verbs
concepts.description: Understanding words that describe how, when, or where an action takes place.
key_ideas: Adverbs of manner (mostly ending in -ly)
Adverbs of time (yesterday, now, soon)
Difference between adjectives and adverbs

concepts.title: Conjunctions — Joining Sentences
concepts.description: Using connecting words to link words, phrases, or short sentences together.
key_ideas: Using 'and' to add information
Using 'but' to show contrast
Using 'or' to show choice
Using 'because' to show reason

concepts.title: Punctuation and Capitalization
concepts.description: Applying correct marks to structure sentences and capitalizing proper nouns.
key_ideas: Capital letters for sentence starts and proper nouns
Full stops and commas
Question marks and exclamation marks

concepts.title: Paragraph Writing
concepts.description: Learn the fundamentals of structuring a single paragraph around one central idea, including a topic sentence and supporting details.
key_ideas: Identifying the main topic or central idea
Writing a clear topic sentence
Using supporting sentences to add details
Writing a concluding sentence

concepts.title: Picture Composition
concepts.description: Develop the ability to observe a visual image and describe the setting, characters, and actions taking place using appropriate vocabulary.
key_ideas: Observing visual details carefully
Using present continuous tense to describe actions
Inferring feelings or context from the image
Organizing observations into a logical sequence

concepts.title: Short Message Writing
concepts.description: Learn to write short, functional notes to convey important information when direct communication is not possible, focusing on brevity and clarity.
key_ideas: Including date and time of the message
Addressing the receiver correctly
Keeping the body brief and to the point
Mentioning the writer's name at the end

concepts.title: Informal Letter Writing
concepts.description: Understand the format and tone required to write personal letters to friends and family members.
key_ideas: Correct placement of sender's address and date
Using appropriate salutations (e.g., Dear...)
Structuring the body into introduction, main message, and conclusion
Using a complimentary close (e.g., Yours lovingly)

concepts.title: Descriptive Writing: People and Places
concepts.description: Practice using adjectives and sensory details to create vivid descriptions of familiar people, pets, or places.
key_ideas: Using adjectives to describe physical appearance
Describing personality traits or atmosphere
Using sensory details (sight, sound, smell)
Creating a mental image for the reader

concepts.title: Prefixes and Suffixes
concepts.description: Prefixes and Suffixes — part of the chapter on Vocabulary.
key_ideas: Core principles of prefixes and suffixes
Step-by-step problem solving for prefixes and suffixes
Real-world applications of prefixes and suffixes

concepts.title: Common Idioms and Phrases
concepts.description: Common Idioms and Phrases — part of the chapter on Vocabulary.
key_ideas: Core principles of common idioms and phrases
Step-by-step problem solving for common idioms and phrases
Real-world applications of common idioms and phrases

concepts.title: Synonyms and Antonyms
concepts.description: Introduction to words that have similar meanings (synonyms) and words that have opposite meanings (antonyms) to enhance descriptive writing.
key_ideas: Synonyms allow for variety in writing to avoid repetition.
Antonyms help express contrast and opposition.
Context determines the best synonym to use.

concepts.title: Homophones and Homonyms
concepts.description: differentiation between words that sound the same but have different spellings and meanings, ensuring correct usage in sentences.
key_ideas: Homophones sound alike but have different spellings (e.g., see/sea, tail/tale).
Homonyms have the same spelling but different meanings (e.g., bark of a tree vs. dog's bark).
Using context clues to determine the correct word choice.

concepts.title: Compound Words
concepts.description: Understanding how two distinct words can be combined to form a new word with a specific meaning.
key_ideas: Closed compounds are written as one word (e.g., keyboard, sunflower).
Open compounds are written as separate words but function as one unit (e.g., ice cream).
Analyzing the meanings of the individual root words to guess the compound meaning.

concepts.title: Using Context Clues
concepts.description: Strategies for determining the meaning of unfamiliar words by analyzing the surrounding text rather than using a dictionary.
key_ideas: Looking for definition clues within the sentence.
Identifying synonym or antonym clues nearby.
Using inference based on the general situation or mood of the text.

concepts.title: One Word Substitution
concepts.description: Learning specific vocabulary words that replace complex phrases or descriptions to make communication more concise.
key_ideas: Replacing descriptive phrases about professions (e.g., 'one who flies planes' -> 'pilot').
Words for groups or collections (collective nouns).
Improving brevity and clarity in writing.
